newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes strong on high money rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes strong on high money rates.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed stronger against the dollar on Wednesday as the rupee came into demand in the wake of volatile money market rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.76 to the U.S. currency after opening at 56.93 and rising to a high of 56.74 during the day.
Overnight call money rates, which have stayed high all week, closed at 24 percent after opening at 23 percent.
"The rupee improved mainly due to pressure from high money market rates," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
High money rates sent traders scrambling to hold long rupee positions, which kept the greenback checked locally despite its strong performance against international currencies, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the Central Bank pushed the dollar up by 0.75 local cents and fixed buying and selling at 55.9325 and 57.0625.
"Money rates are very high. There seems to be a liquidity shortage," a Commercial Bank dealer said. "Some people are looking to the Central Bank to inject liquidity into the market."
